# CsCheck property-based testing (split 4.7.0 / 2.9.0) (tooling)

<!-- Generated by `stackfoundry pack render` from a researched pack. Each rule cites [key] = a source below.
     Disagree with a rule? Record the repo's way in the pack's repoConvention and re-render, so a refresh keeps
     your decision. -->

Applies to: client. Versions in use: 4.7.0 (tests/Transloadit.Tests/Transloadit.Tests.csproj (ItemGroup for net8.0, net9.0, net10.0)); 2.9.0 (tests/Transloadit.Tests/Transloadit.Tests.csproj (ItemGroup for net461, net462, net472, net48, net6.0, net7.0)).

## Rules

- **Keep every CsCheck test source-compatible with both pinned majors: pass Sample options by name (iter:, seed:, threads:, print:), never positionally, and do not use writeLine:, logger:, string-returning (classify) predicates, Gen<T>.Single, Gen.DateTime.Utc/.Local, SampleParallel or SampleModelBasedAsync in shared code.** The same file compiles against 2.9.0 on net461-net7.0 and 4.7.0 on net8.0+. 4.x inserts writeLine as the second Sample parameter (2.9: seed), and the listed APIs exist only in 3.x/4.x, so a test that builds on net8.0 fails to compile on the older TFMs (or the reverse), breaking the whole multi-target build. Here: tests/Transloadit.Tests/Tests/Unit/SignaturePropertyTests.cs (all four Sample calls); tests/Transloadit.Tests/Transloadit.Tests.csproj (the two CsCheck ItemGroups). [src-check-290, src-check-470, nuget-300, nuget-400, nuget-470]
  This repo: The csproj comment states the tests are source compatible with both majors; the existing tests use only Gen.Select, Gen.String, Gen.OneOfConst and Sample(predicate) with defaults.
- **Pass at most 8 generators to one Gen.Select (or Sample tuple); compose larger inputs from nested Select into a record or tuple.** 2.9.0 has Gen.Select overloads up to 16 generators, 4.7.0 only up to 8: a 9+ generator Select written against the old TFMs does not compile on net8.0+. Here: tests/Transloadit.Tests/Tests/Unit/SignaturePropertyTests.cs (Gen.Select with 3 and 4 generators). [src-gen-290, src-gen-470]
- **Declare the character domain explicitly (Gen.String[Gen.Char[...], min, max], Gen.OneOf over Gen.Char ranges) instead of relying on default Gen.String, and include non-ASCII (but no lone surrogates) when the code under test encodes text.** Default Gen.Char differs per major: 2.9.0 emits U+0000-U+007F (NUL and control chars included), 4.7.0 emits only ' '..'~'. The same property therefore tests different inputs per TFM, and neither ever produces non-ASCII, so the UTF-8 multi-byte path of SignatureUtilities.CalculateHash (Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes of input and key) is never exercised by the property tests. Here: tests/Transloadit.Tests/Tests/Unit/SignaturePropertyTests.cs (Gen.String for input and key); src/Transloadit/Utilities/SignatureUtilities.cs (CalculateHash). [src-gen-290, src-gen-470, readme]
- **Assert only what the algorithm guarantees; exclude the known equivalence classes in the generator or the guard. For HMAC keys, 'different key implies different signature' does not hold for keys that differ only by trailing NUL bytes (short keys are zero-padded to the block size) or for strings whose invalid surrogates UTF-8-encode to the same replacement bytes.** Signature_WithADifferentKey only skips key == otherKey. With 2.9.0's default Gen.Char (NUL possible) or a widened alphabet, a pair like 'k' and 'k' + NUL validates, the test fails rarely and only on some TFMs, and the failure looks like an auth bug in production code when the property itself is false. Here: tests/Transloadit.Tests/Tests/Unit/SignaturePropertyTests.cs (Signature_WithADifferentKey_DoesNotValidate). [rfc2104, src-gen-290]
- **Pair each property whose two sides share the code under test with an independent oracle (pinned vectors, a second implementation), and generate mutations rather than appending a fixed suffix.** Signature_RoundTrips calls CalculateSignature and ValidateSignature, which both run the same CalculateHash, and Signature_IsDeterministic calls one pure function twice: a wrong hash, key encoding or hex casing passes both. Signature_OverTamperedInput only checks input + "x". The hash itself is guarded only by the ASCII pinned vectors in SignatureTests; on an auth path that leaves non-ASCII encoding unproven. Here: tests/Transloadit.Tests/Tests/Unit/SignaturePropertyTests.cs (Signature_RoundTrips_ForAnyInputAndKey, Signature_IsDeterministic, Signature_OverTamperedInput_DoesNotValidate); tests/Transloadit.Tests/Tests/SignatureTests.cs (TestCalculateSignature pinned vectors). [wlaschin-properties]
- **Reproduce a failure with the printed seed (CsCheck_Seed environment variable or a temporary seed: argument) on the same TFM group that failed, then pin the shrunk values as an example-based [Fact]/[InlineData]; do not commit seed: as the regression guard.** A seed only replays the same values under the same CsCheck version and generator definitions: 2.9.0 and 4.7.0 generate different strings from the same Gen.String, and 5.0.0 changed seeds for Gen.Decimal/Double/Float. A seed from a net48 run replays nothing on net8.0, and a committed seed silently stops covering the case after an upgrade. Here: tests/Transloadit.Tests/Tests/Unit/SignaturePropertyTests.cs. [readme, src-check-290, nuget-500, src-gen-290, src-gen-470]
- **Leave iter: and time: at their defaults in committed tests (100 iterations, Check.Iter) and raise depth for a dedicated run with CsCheck_Iter / CsCheck_Time.** CI runs each TFM sequentially (max-parallel: 1, 3 Linux + 3 Windows jobs) together with live API tests; a hardcoded time: adds that many seconds per test per TFM, and a large iter: multiplies across every TFM in the matrix. Here: .github/workflows/tests.yml (test-linux, test-netfx); tests/Transloadit.Tests/Tests/Unit/SignaturePropertyTests.cs. [readme, src-check-290, src-check-470]
- **Build every fixture (client, FakeHttpMessageHandler, CapturingHandler, culture) inside the predicate; never assert on a handler or client shared across Sample iterations.** Sample runs the predicate on Check.Threads threads (default: logical CPU count); xUnit's DisableTestParallelization does not limit it. Single-slot captures such as FakeHttpMessageHandler.LastRequestContent or CapturingHandler.LastResponseBody are overwritten by another iteration, giving flaky failures on the wrong input. On 2.9.0 every worker runs on the thread pool even with threads: 1 (calling-thread execution came later, issue #12), so thread-affine ambient state set by the test (Thread.CurrentThread.CurrentCulture as in CultureRobustnessTests.RunInCulture, [ThreadStatic]) cannot be assumed to reach the predicate. Here: not used here yet; tests/Transloadit.Tests/Infrastructure/FakeHttpMessageHandler.cs (LastRequestContent); tests/Transloadit.Tests/Infrastructure/CapturingHandler.cs (LastResponseBody); tests/Transloadit.Tests/Tests/Unit/CultureRobustnessTests.cs (RunInCulture). [readme, src-check-290, src-check-470, issue-12]
- **Build valid values with Select/ranges instead of Where filters that reject often.** 2.9.0's Where retries forever (the net461-net7.0 test run hangs), while 4.7.0 throws after Check.WhereLimit (default 100) consecutive rejections: the same test hangs on one TFM group and fails on the other. Here: not used here yet. [src-gen-290, src-gen-470, src-check-470]
- **For serialization round-trip properties, generate values at the wire's precision and domain: bounded Gen.Double[a, b] (no NaN/Infinity), DateTime from Gen.DateTime[start, finish] truncated to whole seconds with an explicit Kind, and run them through TestSerializer.Default so each TFM exercises its own engine.** Default Gen.Double (2.9.0) maps raw bit patterns, so it emits NaN and Infinity, which are not JSON numbers; default Gen.DateTime has Kind Unspecified and full tick precision, while the wire date format is second-precision with an offset ('2025/02/20 01:52:04+00:00'). Without this the property fails on generator noise instead of the asymmetric read/write mappings it should catch. Gen.DateTime.Utc/Local exist only in 4.x. Here: not used here yet; tests/Transloadit.Tests/Tests/Unit/RoundTripStabilityTests.cs (AssertStableRoundTrip, example-based today); tests/Transloadit.Tests/Infrastructure/TestSerializer.cs (TestSerializer.Default). [src-gen-290, src-gen-470, rfc8259]

## Bug categories

| Category | Look for | Failure |
|---|---|---|
| `cross-major-api` (blocker) | In a CsCheck test: positional Sample arguments after the predicate, writeLine:/logger:, string-returning predicates, Single, Gen.DateTime.Utc/Local, SampleParallel, SampleModelBasedAsync, more than 8 generators in one Select, without a TFM guard. | Compile error on one TFM group (net461-net7.0 with 2.9.0 or net8.0+ with 4.7.0), breaking the multi-target build or the CI leg that builds it. [src-check-290, src-check-470, src-gen-290, src-gen-470] |
| `false-property` (confirm) | Inequality or uniqueness properties over hashes, HMACs, encodings or normalisation whose guard only excludes exact equality of the generated inputs. | Rare, TFM-dependent failure that blames correct production code (e.g. two keys differing by trailing NUL produce the same HMAC). [rfc2104] |
| `tautological-property` (confirm) | Round-trip or determinism properties where both sides call the same function under test, with no pinned vector or independent oracle covering the same domain. | A wrong signature, encoding or serializer mapping passes the property; on the auth path an incorrect signature ships. [wlaschin-properties] |
| `generator-domain-gap` (confirm) | Default Gen.String/Gen.Char used where non-ASCII, empty, long or boundary values matter; default Gen.Double/Gen.DateTime fed to a JSON round trip. | The property passes while the interesting inputs (non-ASCII UTF-8, NaN, sub-second dates) are never generated, or fails on values the wire format cannot carry. [src-gen-290, src-gen-470, rfc8259] |
| `shared-state-across-iterations` (confirm) | A handler, client, list, static field or ambient culture created outside the Sample predicate and read inside it. | Flaky failure or false pass because parallel iterations overwrite single-slot captures, or ambient thread state never reaches CsCheck's worker threads. [readme, issue-12, src-check-290] |
| `unbounded-where` (blocker) | Where(...) on a generator whose predicate rejects most values (e.g. equality to another generated value, narrow ranges). | Hang on 2.9.0 TFMs (no retry limit) and CsCheckException on 4.7.0 TFMs after 100 rejections. [src-gen-290, src-gen-470] |

## Testing

CsCheck property tests are offline unit tests in tests/Transloadit.Tests/Tests/Unit, run on every test TFM (2.9.0 on net461-net7.0, 4.7.0 on net8.0+). They prove invariants over generated inputs; exact outputs (signature hashes, wire JSON) stay with pinned example tests (SignatureTests, golden/snapshot tests).

- Harness: tests/Transloadit.Tests/Tests/Unit/SignaturePropertyTests.cs (SignaturePropertyTests: static Gen fields + one [Fact] per property calling Sample); tests/Transloadit.Tests/Infrastructure/TestSerializer.cs (TestSerializer.Default, the per-TFM serializer for round-trip properties); tests/Transloadit.Tests/Transloadit.Tests.csproj (CsCheck ItemGroups)
- Run: `dotnet test tests/Transloadit.Tests/Transloadit.Tests.csproj -f net8.0 --filter "FullyQualifiedName~SignaturePropertyTests"`; `dotnet test tests/Transloadit.Tests/Transloadit.Tests.csproj -f net48 --filter "FullyQualifiedName~SignaturePropertyTests"`; `PowerShell reproduce: $env:CsCheck_Seed = "<seed from failure>"; dotnet test tests/Transloadit.Tests/Transloadit.Tests.csproj -f <failing tfm> --filter "FullyQualifiedName~<Test>"; Remove-Item Env:CsCheck_Seed`; `PowerShell deep run: $env:CsCheck_Iter = "100000"; dotnet test tests/Transloadit.Tests/Transloadit.Tests.csproj -f net8.0 --filter "FullyQualifiedName~PropertyTests"; Remove-Item Env:CsCheck_Iter`
- Shuffled: `CsCheck draws a fresh random seed every run unless CsCheck_Seed or seed: is set, so property tests vary run to run by design; a failure is only reproducible from its printed seed on the same TFM group.`
- Trap: Run a new property on one net8.0+ TFM and one 2.9.0 TFM (net48 or net462): the two majors generate different inputs and expose different APIs.
- Trap: CI covers 2.9.0 only on net462/net472/net48; net461, net6.0 and net7.0 are built locally only.
- Trap: CsCheck_Seed applies to every Sample in the process; always combine it with a --filter for the one failing test.
- Trap: Failure output prints the shrunk inputs; keep generated values free of real secrets.
- Sources: [readme, src-check-290, src-check-470, src-gen-290, src-gen-470]

## Performance

- Sample defaults: 100 iterations on Environment.ProcessorCount threads. Signature properties are cheap at that size; serializer round-trip properties over large models cost per iteration, so bound collection sizes (default Array/List length is 0-127) rather than lowering iter. Here: tests/Transloadit.Tests/Tests/Unit/SignaturePropertyTests.cs. [readme, src-check-290, src-gen-470]

## Security

- Never feed the real AuthKey/AuthSecret from appsettings.Tests.json (or CI secrets) into a property: on failure CsCheck appends the printed shrunk input to the exception message, which lands in CI logs. Generate keys instead, as SignaturePropertyTests does. Here: tests/Transloadit.Tests/Tests/Unit/SignaturePropertyTests.cs; .github/workflows/tests.yml (Create Test Settings). [src-check-290, readme]
- No GitHub security advisories exist for the CsCheck NuGet package (searched 2026-11-09). The package has no dependencies in either pinned version. [ghsa, nuget-290, nuget-470]

## Upgrades

- Pinned in: CsCheck 4.7.0: tests/Transloadit.Tests/Transloadit.Tests.csproj, ItemGroup net8.0/net9.0/net10.0; CsCheck 2.9.0: tests/Transloadit.Tests/Transloadit.Tests.csproj, ItemGroup net461/net462/net472/net48/net6.0/net7.0
- Moves with: The two CsCheck pins must stay source compatible with one shared test source; bump either only after compiling all test TFMs.; 4.9.1 is the last version targeting net8.0; 5.x targets net10.0/net11.0 only, so adopting 5.x would mean a third CsCheck version (net10.0) beside 4.9.x (net8.0/net9.0) and 2.x.; 5.0.0 turns Array/List/HashSet/ArrayUnique into extension properties; the test project uses LangVersion 12, so check that these still compile before adopting 5.x (consuming C# 14 extension members is not verified under LangVersion 12).
- Release notes: https://www.nuget.org/packages/CsCheck/4.7.0 · https://www.nuget.org/packages/CsCheck/4.9.1 · https://www.nuget.org/packages/CsCheck/5.0.0 · https://www.nuget.org/packages/CsCheck/5.0.1 · https://www.nuget.org/packages/CsCheck/2.9.0 · https://www.nuget.org/packages/CsCheck/2.14.1
- Migration guides: https://www.nuget.org/packages/CsCheck/3.0.0 · https://www.nuget.org/packages/CsCheck/4.0.0 · https://www.nuget.org/packages/CsCheck/5.0.0
- Deprecated APIs still in use: Gen.OneOfConst (SignaturePropertyTests.Algorithms): present and not obsolete in 2.9.0 and 4.7.0, removed in 5.0.0 in favour of a Gen.OneOf constants overload that 2.9.0/4.7.0 lack. Portable form across 2.9/4.7: Gen.OneOf(Gen.Const(a), Gen.Const(b), ...); confirm it still compiles on 5.x before upgrading.

## Not reached

- CsCheck GitHub Releases and tags: the repository publishes none, so release notes come from NuGet version pages and the 2.9.0/4.7.0 sources were matched to commits by date and release-note text, not by tag.
- The exact seed-message text of 4.7.0 (SampleErrorMessage body was outside the fetched excerpts); the README (5.x) and 2.9.0 source show 'Set seed: "..." or CsCheck_Seed=... to reproduce'.
- 5.x source for Gen.Const and Gen.OneOf(params IGen<T>[]) was not checked, so the portable OneOfConst replacement is verified only for 2.9.0 and 4.7.0.
- Whether consuming 5.0's C# 14 extension properties compiles under LangVersion 12: the C# 14 page does not state it.
